item.title: [pnpm/pnpm] pnpm 12.22.0 (v12.22.0)
item.description:
pnpm 12.22.0 adds a `globalPackagesConfig` section to the global `config.yaml` for settings that apply only to global packages, adds `pnpm why --ranges`, and lists workspace projects in dependency order in `pnpm list --recursive`. It also includes a security fix. After the default or a scoped registry changed, `pnpm install` could skip the `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` checks against the new registry.

`pnpm approve-builds -g` and `pnpm add -g --allow-build` now save build decisions under `globalPackagesConfig.permissions`. pnpm still applies build settings from the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` of the global packages directory, with a deprecation warning. The next ap

item.title: [solidjs/solid] v2.0.0 - The Long Hold (solid-js@2.0.0)
item.description:
# Solid 2.0 is here
5 years is a long time to work on anything. Solid 1.0 bet on signals at a time when fine-grained reactivity was a rare position. Today you will find it in Angular, Svelte, Vue Vapor and a TC39 proposal. Solid 2.0 takes the next step, and today it reaches stable.
### 📣 Read the announcement: Solid 2.0 - The Long Hold
## What 2.0 brings
- **Async in the graph.** A computation can return a Promise or an async iterator, and everything downstream just handles it. Race conditions are taken care of, optimistic state rolls back so the server stays the source of truth, and `live` streams server functions over persistent connections. Adding async does not mean refactoring your app. - **Built to be written by agents.** A fine-grained graph knows exactly what was read, where, and what will update. Development builds report reactive mistakes with a stable code, a source location and a fix, and the same graph catches waterfalls, runaway effects and fan-out that will

item.title: [bluesky-social/atproto] @atproto/oauth-provider@0.26.0
item.description:
### Minor Changes
- #5919 `8d84a6c` Thanks @matthieusieben! - Upgrade `ioredis` to 6.x. By default, the Redis clients these packages create stay on RESP2 and skip `CLIENT SETINFO` on connect, as with `ioredis` 5, and take `ioredis` 6's other new defaults:
- `family` is `0` (was `4`): hostnames resolve to IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, not only IPv4. - `retryStrategy` waits 50ms × 2^(attempt − 1), up to 5s, plus up to 200ms of jitter, between reconnection attempts (was 50ms × attempt, up to 2s). - `keepAlive` is `30000`: TCP keepalive probes start after 30s of idle (was off).
The `redis` option of `OAuthProvider` now expects an `ioredis` 6 `Redis` instance, which is used as is, or `RedisOptions`, which can override these defaults.
### Patch Changes
- Updated dependencies : - @atproto/lex-resolver@0.4.6

item.title: [anomalyco/opentui] Release v0.9.0 (v0.9.0)
item.description:
In 0.9.0, Markdown runs on OpenTUI's native engine, the same engine the Rust widget uses. In 0.8.3, `MarkdownRenderable` parsed with `marked` in JavaScript and lexed the open end of the document again on every chunk. In a growing list, the open end is the whole list, so streaming one list took 21,430 million instructions. `MarkdownRenderable` also sent all prose to the Tree-sitter worker for styling. The native engine reads each chunk once and writes paragraphs and headings into their text nodes itself. Streaming the same list now takes 5.9 million instructions. Over one streamed answer, JavaScript's styled-text writes for prose went from 1,595 to 0, and the prose characters sent to the highlighter went from 56,223 to 0.
Because the engine follows CommonMark 0.31.2 and GFM, some documents look different. While streaming, a line that can still change kind, such as a possible table row or a heading underline, waits for its end before it shows. A table appears when its delimiter row arri

## Protect private forks when deleting repositories
`gh repo delete` now warns when deleting a private or internal repository will also delete its forks. The additional confirmation is required even with `--yes`.
Non-interactive workflows and agents must explicitly accept the cascading deletion:
```shell gh repo delete OWNER/REPO --yes --accept-cascading-deletion-of-private-forks ```

item.title: [mongodb/node-mongodb-native] v7.9.0
item.description:
## 7.9.0 (2026-11-12)
The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 7.9.0 of the `mongodb` package!
## Release Notes
> [!WARNING] > Node Driver versions from 6.7.0 before 7.9.0 (this release) are affected by a security issue related to OIDC bearer tokens being inappropriately shared to domains outside those allowlisted by the application (CVE-2026-126835). item.title: [nanaism/yomiyasu] v3.1.0
item.description:
yomiyasu v3.1.0 を公開しました。 スキルのフォルダから Codex 用のプラグインの設定を外したバージョンです。 Codex にスキルのフォルダを写して入れている方は、スキルの名前が `yomiyasu:yomiyasu` から `yomiyasu` に変わります。更新したあとに書き換える所は、下の「Codex で使っている方へ」にあります。 名前が変わるので、パッチではなくマイナーバージョンにしています。 推敲の手順（SKILL.md と references）は、SKILL.md のバージョンの行を除いて v3.0.1 から変えていません。 lint、diff、check、フックの出力も、JSON の `tool_version` と `--version` が示すバージョンを除いて v3.0.1 と同じです。
## 背景と課題
パッケージマネージャーの apm で yomiyasu をプロジェクトに入れようとすると失敗する、という報告をいただきました（Hol1kgmg さんの issue #61）。
apm は、依存先を `nanaism/yomiyasu/skills/yomiyasu` のようにフォルダまで書くと、そのフォルダの中身だけを見て種類を決めます。 apm 0.35.0 からは、フォルダに `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` があると、SKILL.md より先にこれを見て「Codex のプラグイン」と決めるようになりました。 apm は Codex のプラグインをユーザー単位でしか入れない決まりにしているので、プロジェクト単位の `apm install` が止まります。
このファイルは v2.0.2 で置いたもので、Codex でのスキルの名前を `yomiyasu:yomiyasu` にするための、名前だけの設定です。 yomiyasu はこれまで、スキルの名前を「バージョンを上げても変えないもの」として扱ってきました。 名前を保つかぎり、スキルのフォルダは「スキルでもプラグインでもあるもの」のまま残ります。
